chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the forearm when it is struck and the wrist bone fractures from it. He said: 'If the hand becomes withered/paralyzed from it, or all the fingers of the hand become immobile, then in it is two-thirds of the blood money of the hand.' He said: 'And if some of the fingers become immobile and some remain, then for each finger that becomes immobile, two-thirds of its blood money is applicable.' He said: 'And the same ruling applies to the leg and the foot if the toes of the foot become immobile.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for blood money when a hand or foot becomes paralyzed due to injury?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides precise jurisprudential criteria for *diyah* (blood money) based on functional loss rather than mere physical damage, establishing that total hand paralysis warrants two-thirds of the hand's value. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on practical utility in compensation, a principle later refined by scholars like al-Murtada and al-Majlisi to distinguish between complete and partial impairment. The extension of this logic to the toes underscores the systematic nature of Shia *fiqh* in applying proportional justice to bodily injuries.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5301 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a forearm (the arm below the elbow) that was struck and resulted in the fracture of the wrist bone.

Imam (as) replied: If the hand becomes paralyzed or all the fingers of the hand become immobile due to the injury, then two-thirds of the blood money (diyyah) of the entire hand is applicable.
Imam (as) further stated: If only some of the fingers become paralyzed while others remain functional, then for each finger that becomes paralyzed, two-thirds of its individual diyyah is applicable. The same ruling applies to the leg and foot if the toes of the foot become paralyzed.
